findings.text: Two macro families construct read modify write operations that expose condition codes. Binary forms take an operation, a memory location, a condition selector, a value constraint and a value, with one spelling supplying a default destination template. Suffixed forms append a follow up operation and accept additional clobbers. All declare memory clobbered and bind the value operand through a shared core.

Virtualization tolerant spinning exposes an enabled predicate consulting a static branch key and a lock helper taking a resilient lock pointer and returning integer status through a test and set primitive. The public lock type has two alternative aliases, one naming the generic queue lock structure and one naming a resilient specific structure.
Each examined x86 header guards against multiple inclusion with a distinct preprocessor symbol defined once near the file start.

Loader information is a packed record with coarse alignment. It starts with words for interface version, attributes, vendor identity and build date. Narrow fields then carry build number plus minor, major and update revisions. Further words give APIC identity and remaining update count. A large opaque byte area follows for loader data. The tail holds single byte ready and debug flags, a physical ready flag, and extensive reserved padding.

Filtering identifies native audit architecture, call count and readable name, with one triple for 64 bit native, one for 32 bit native, and a compat triple for 32 bit calls under 64 bit. Native signal return aliases normal signal return. The four 32 bit numbers for read, write, exit and signal return alias the corresponding IA32 numbers.
A descriptor builder merges base, limit and flag inputs into one descriptor word by placing low and high slices of each input at separate bit positions with masking.

Selector decoding reserves low bits for privilege and table choice. Masks isolate privilege level and table selection, with defined values for user privilege, user segment filtering, local versus global table, and a zero index for invalid segments. Boot code, data and task entries use indices 2, 3 and 4, with selectors formed by scaling the index to selector granularity.

The larger table has 32 entries. Thread local storage starts at index 6 and spans 3 entries. Kernel code is at 12 with data at 13. Default user code is at 14 with data at 15. Task state is at 16 with descriptor table at 17. Firmware and power management occupy 18 through 23. Fixup stack is at 26, per CPU at 27, node at 28, and double fault task at 31. Selectors scale the index by 8, adding privilege 3 for user and node selectors.

The smaller table has 16 entries. Kernel 32 bit code is at 1, kernel code at 2, kernel data at 3. User 32 bit code is at 4, user data at 5, user code at 6. Task state is at 8 and descriptor table at 10. Thread local entries are 12 through 14 with node at 15. Selectors again scale by 8 with privilege 3 added for user and node selectors.

Interrupt and table sizing fixes 256 IDT slots with 32 exception vectors and a defined error code mask. Total descriptor table bytes equal entries times 8. Thread local storage uses 3 entries with size 24 bytes. Node plus CPU packing reserves 12 low bits for CPU with matching mask. Early handler size adds a constant 9, or 8 under Xen, to the branch terminator size.

Node and CPU packing shifts the node value above the CPU field and merges the CPU number. Reading splits the packed value back into optional CPU and node outputs after loading it from the node selector through a segment limit read, substituted by a processor identity read when that feature is present.

Segment helpers are generated per named register. Loading uses a volatile move guarded by an exception entry that zeroes the destination on fault and treats memory as clobbered. Saving uses a volatile move into a general register and returns the value as an unsigned long.

Descriptor construction truncates oversized inputs by masking, so callers must bound base, limit and flags beforehand. Firmware code testing masks selector bits before comparison against the 32 bit code selector.

Serial defaults derive the base rate from 1843200 divided by 16. Common port flags combine boot autoconfiguration with test skipping and possibly automatic interrupt assignment, with the fourth port using a distinct spelling. Four legacy entries map ttyS0 through ttyS3 to ports 0x3F8, 0x2F8, 0x3E8 and 0x2E8 with interrupts 4, 3, 4 and 3 respectively.

Boot sizing fixes command line at 2048 bytes, boot parameter block at 4096 bytes, and low memory at 0x9f000. Old command line uses magic 0xA33F at offset 0x020 with new pointer at 0x228 relative to real mode data. Maximum memory frame derives from MAXMEM, while the non PAE frame limit is 1 shifted by 20.
Three early platform hooks for generic virtualization, Intel mobile and CE4100 are empty inline routines that boot code may call unconditionally.

Randomized layout status requires both the memory randomization build option and a load flag in boot parameters. Memory randomization further requires sanitizer absence. The runtime offset is the distance between the running text address and its link base. The builtin command line marker is zero.
Boot time heap reservation has two spellings, one emitting a one byte aligned used character array in a dedicated section and one delegating to a shared reservation helper with name and size.
A self naming definition marks the read only plus execute mapping helper as present on this architecture.

PCI option ROM handoff starts with a setup data header, then vendor and device identifiers plus a length. Address fields for segment, bus, device and function follow as machine words, ending with trailing variable ROM bytes. EFI handoff holds vendor, an unused word, table and SMBIOS addresses, then eight reserved words.

Guest hypervisor messaging reserves the low 12 bits for request identity starting at bit 0, with a mask covering those bits and payload recovered by shifting right by 12. SEV information uses response 0x001 and request 0x002, packing maximum version high, then minimum version, then encryption bit position, plus the response tag.

CPUID proxy uses request 0x004 and response 0x005. Function and value occupy the high 32 bits, register selector occupies bits near 30 with two bit mask, and register identities map 0 through 3 to AX, BX, CX and DX. Requests merge register and function with the tag. Reset hold uses 0x006 and 0x007 with result at bit 12. Prefetch uses 0x010 and 0x011 with address at bit 12 and an all ones none value. Registration uses 0x012 and 0x013.

Page state operations number private as 1 and shared as 2 in both enum and exit code forms. Single page messaging uses request 0x014 packing operation near bit 52 with frame number from bit 12, plus extractors for each field, and response 0x015 with value taken from the high half. Error combines the top bit with the response tag. Privilege level messaging uses 0x016 and 0x017 with level carried near bit 32. Feature discovery uses 0x080 and 0x081 with bitmap from bit 12, flagging SNP, AP creation and multi level support.

Batched page state change uses a packed header with current and end indices plus reserved space. Each packed entry carries a 12 bit sub page field, a 40 bit frame number, a 4 bit operation, a page size flag and reserved bits. The descriptor pairs one header with 64 entries. Limits allow 64 entries per descriptor and 253 pages per call, with distinct codes for generic, header and entry failures.

Batched changes progress by advancing the header current index toward the end index across calls, with header and entry errors aborting the batch. Single message exchanges pair each even request tag with the next response tag, while termination is one way and conveys a reason set plus reason value.

Termination uses request 0x100, carrying a 4 bit set from bit 12 and an 8 bit reason from bit 16. Generic set 0 covers general request, unsupported protocol and unsupported SNP. Linux set 1 numbers failures for registration, page change, validation, privilege level, CPUID paths, secrets page, service module presence and configuration, secure time, remapping and secure interrupt controllers. Hypervisor replies are 0 idle, 1 raise exception and 2 malformed input.
